title: The youth department's targets: how many programs met them
question: Did youth programs reach the number of participants they projected and the results the department set as targets?
finding: In 2025-26, 181 of 215 programs met the enrolment target (at least 90% of the participants each program projected), so 34 fell short; strategy averages run as high as 200% of projection, so some programs served far more than they projected. Programs met 45% of outcome targets (grades, credentials, assessments and the like), 79% of the required mid-year and year-end narrative reports, and 64% of survey targets. Weakest outcome results: Academic Supports: Percent of participants who have a completed individual learning plan. (7 of 14 met, average 64% against a 85% target); Academic Supports: Percent of participants who pass their courses. (Disconnected transitional-age young adults (TAY/A) Only) (0 of 2 met, average 27% against a 75% target); Alternative Education: Percent of participants who have a completed individual learning plan. (2 of 5 met, average 71% against a 85% target).
how: Each report's performance-measure table (target, number of programs, number that met the target, average result) was read line by line; a measure is labelled enrolment, report, survey, quality process or outcome from its wording.
limits: The table counts programs that reported; those that reported nothing are left out of the average, as the report notes. A missed survey or report target is a paperwork result, not a finding about services. Programs are not named, so a strategy figure cannot be tied to a grantee.
